findings.description: Tax is really TWO distinct typed ranges, not the single flat 'Tax' tab the EARS enumeration ('four ... tabs — Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax') implies. Real code: TaxView{accruals: ViewTab (name=TAX_TAB, header=TAX_HEADER: Sale ID/Lot ID/Jurisdiction/Tax Year/Amount/Lifecycle State), reserve_summary: ViewTab (name=TAX_RESERVE_TAB='Tax · Reserve Summary', header=TAX_RESERVE_HEADER: Jurisdiction/Tax Year/Accrued/Moved/Paid/Outstanding/Shortfall)}, with tests (tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows) explicitly asserting the two bands are distinct, separately named, separately headered, and never merged. Forced only to the spec text, all three A sketches invent a SINGLE flat Tax entity with placeholder columns unrelated to the real schema (A1: Year/ST Gain/LT Gain; A2: TaxRow{tax_year, short_term_gain, long_term_gain}; A3: elided). All three B reconstructions independently surface the accrual/reserve-summary split as a first-class, heavily-emphasized requirement. Same root gap visible from both directions: the 'four tabs' framing hides a real fifth published range.

The four tabs' exact column schemas are pinned constants/tests with no trace in the EARS text, which only says 'typed headers': POSITIONS_HEADER is 13 columns (Symbol, Shares, Avg Cost/Share, Total Basis, Price, Market Value, Unrealized P&L, Est. Tax Rate, Est. Unrealized Tax (est), Net Unrealized (est), Unrealized %, Realized P&L, Quote Date); OPEN_LOTS_HEADER is 10 (incl. Source, Platform, Tracking Code, Term); REALIZED_HEADER is 11 (incl. Holding Days, Term, State, Tax Year). All three A sketches invent materially thinner, unrelated schemas (e.g. A1's 3-column Positions header of Symbol/Quantity/Market Value vs. the real 13) — the spec is silent on column content, so B's exact pinned schema is pure code-side surplus, unanimous across B1/B2/B3.

workbook_tab_order() pins a whole-workbook tab ordering that SHEET-TAB-001's text never addresses: the four view tabs, then HISTORY_TAB, then config tabs (TAX_RULES_TAB, RESIDENCY_TAB, PLATFORMS_ALIASES_TAB), then event logs (LEDGER_EVENTS_TAB, TAX_EVENTS_TAB) last — with Positions pinned as the leftmost/landing tab — reasserted idempotently via set_tab_order on every republish (tested by workbook_order_views_then_config_then_logs_positions_landing and republish_idempotently_reasserts_tab_order). The EARS text concerns only the four tabs' internal row/header shape, never their position among the other six workbook tabs sheets-view doesn't even own. Unanimous across B1/B2/B3.

The republish mechanism pins a frozen-header/tail-truncate contract nowhere implied by 'typed headers ... no among-data summary rows': row 1 is written exactly once and NEVER rewritten on any later republish (SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view doc contract); only the data range from DATA_START_ROW=2 down is rewritten as one atomic update, tail-truncating any residual rows to the new exact count — pinned directly by the test republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header. Unanimous across B1/B2/B3, though B1 alone adds the granular settle-pass column-index detail (Symbol=col 0, Price=col 4, Quote Date=col 12).

ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(Symbol) is a hard, explicit error contract with no basis in the EARS text: if Snapshot.positions ever carried two entries for one symbol, render_positions aborts with Err(DuplicateSymbolRow) instead of silently emitting/merging a duplicate row — kept as a defensive assertion even though the real Map-keyed Snapshot.positions makes it structurally unreachable today (per the code's own comment). Called out as an explicit 'Unwanted behavior' EARS bullet in all three B reconstructions (B2 additionally notes the 'structurally unreachable ... defensive' nuance).

'Read-only' cashes out as always-overwrite-by-design rather than any Sheets-level protection: any human-inserted or edited row inside a tab's data range is silently discarded on the next republish (full data-range rewrite, no merge/preserve), demonstrated by the test republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header (v2 republish with fewer rows silently truncates v1's extra row). B2 and B3 state this as an explicit unwanted-behavior EARS rule; B1 only implies it via the 'tail-truncating' republish description without stating the human-edit-discard consequence directly — a minor point of B-run divergence in framing, not substance.

All three A sketches converge on inventing an explicit per-column declared-type mechanism to satisfy 'typed headers' — A1's ColumnType enum + ColumnSpec{name, ty}, A2's Cell enum tied to a SheetRow::headers()/cells() trait, A3's ColumnHeader{name, kind: ColumnKind} — i.e. a structural type tag living at the header/column level. The real ViewTab.header is a bare Vec<String> with no declared-type structure at all; typing for Sheets' filter/sort is instead achieved implicitly through careful value-string formatting (e.g. '20.0000%' via fmt_ppm, '150.00' via fmt_cents) relying on Sheets' userEnteredValue auto-detection, plus the row-level Cell::Value/Cell::Formula split (which encodes the engine-value/live-formula boundary, not column typing). No B run calls out this specific absence, so it stands as an A-side-only observation traceable to the literal spec phrase 'typed headers.'

notes: Grounded in direct reads of sheets-view/src/lib.rs, sheets-view/tests/tabs.rs, runtime/src/adapters.rs, runtime/src/sheets.rs, runtime/tests/cold_start.rs. Primary drift is the Tax accrual/reserve-summary two-band split (BD): the EARS text's flat 'four tabs' enumeration forces all three A sketches to invent a single flat Tax entity with invented columns, while all three B reconstructions independently surface the real two-range split (TAX_TAB vs TAX_RESERVE_TAB='Tax · Reserve Summary') as a headline requirement. Beyond that shared gap, B surfaces several additional code-pinned mechanisms with no spec-text trace (exact header schemas, whole-workbook tab ordering, frozen-header/tail-truncate republish contract, DuplicateSymbolRow hard error, overwrite-by-design semantics for 'read-only'), and A surfaces one softer spec-traced-but-uncorroborated observation (all three sketches invent a declared per-column type tag for 'typed headers' that the real code doesn't have, relying instead on implicit Sheets value-string typing). Both direction sets are internally consistent (high/high), with only minor scope/depth differences within each (A2 alone models a publish/write path; B1 alone gives settle-pass column indices; B3 alone reaches into stale-banner/republish-failure handling).
